def DState.init (statics : Statics) : DState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0⟩

/-- The `n` cells from position `b` of the stack, leaves of the administered storage (§46; DS-v1,
non-normative). -/
def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n

/-- The cells above mark `m` (DS-v1, non-normative, "a cell above m"; reading recorded; §46
available leaves): the positions from the top of `m` to the current top, those that `rewind m`
returns to available. -/
def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := cellsOf st m.top (st.top - m.top)

/-- The stack seen as an administration entry (§46, §36; DS-v1, non-normative): storage,
`internal`, available cells (positions `≥ top`) and issued blocks. Used for `MetaRight` and the
static checks of the derived `issue`, which read only the storage and `internal`. -/
def Stack.entry (st : Stack) : ArenaEntry :=
  ⟨st.storage, st.internal, st.cells.drop st.top,
    st.blocks.map fun x => (cellsOf st x.base x.size, x.auth)⟩

/-- The block of the stack whose authority is `b` (§46 issuances; DS-v1, non-normative). -/
def Stack.block (st : Stack) (b : Nat) : Option Blk := st.blocks.find? fun y => decide (y.auth = b)

/-- A live mark of stack `j` (DS-v1, non-normative: a mark that is neither dead nor foreign; it
decides the `fail` case of `rewind`, §58): it names stack `j` and belongs to its list of live
marks. -/
def LiveMark (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop := m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks

/-- Decidability of `LiveMark` (§58; DS-v1). -/
instance (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Decidable (LiveMark j st m) := by
  unfold LiveMark; infer_instance

/-- The administrative right of §36 for a stack (DS-v1, non-normative, with §36 and §46 read for a
stack): the stack is live (`internal` is active) and `MetaRight`, `Modify` exercisable on the stack
value, the place holding `internal`. -/
def AdminRight (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Prop := s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRight s st.entry

/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; DS-v1). -/
instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Decidable (AdminRight s st) := by
  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance

/-! ## `newStack` and the guard of §56 -/

/-- The stack registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; DS-v1, non-normative): the
`internal` identities of its live stacks. -/
def stackInternals (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) : List Nat :=
  (stacks.filter fun st => decide (s.Active st.internal)).map (·.internal)

----
def rewindMeta (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Stack :=
  { st with
    top := m.top
    blocks := st.blocks.filter fun x => decide (x.base < m.top)
    marks := st.marks.takeWhile fun x => decide (x ≠ m) }

/-- `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v1, non-normative): `fail`, the state unchanged, on a dead or foreign mark;
`reject` without the administrative right of §36; then the derived `reset` of Part XIV on the cells
above `m` (reading recorded): `split` of `internal` on them (O2), which rejects when an active
authority derived from `internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`), and `release`
of the derived authority (O3); `ok`: the cells return to available, `m` and the later marks are
removed. -/
inductive RewindStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → RewindStep k j m D .reject
  | dead {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ LiveMark j st m → RewindStep k j m D .fail
  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m → ¬ AdminRight D.kern st →
      RewindStep k j m D .reject
  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m → AdminRight D.kern st →
      SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
  | release {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m →
      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m →
      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      RewindStep k j m D (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (rewindMeta st m), D.fresh⟩)

/-! ## `grow` (DS-v1: in place, the derived `issue`) -/

/-- In-place extension (DS-v1, non-normative: "extension into the space directly after the
block"; the availability check of the derived `issue`, §77.4): the block ends at the top, and
`extra` available cells follow it. -/
def InPlace (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Prop :=
  x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ st.top + extra ≤ st.cells.length

/-- Decidability of `InPlace` (§77.4; DS-v1). -/
----

      · exact hb q z hz
  | @store a p hs =>
    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
    have hd := hp.derivedHeld

        · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hz]; exact lt_of_getElem? hy
      · exact hb q z hz

/-- Every kernel-reachable state satisfies `DBound` (support for DS-v1, non-normative; §47: no
anchor initially; §57 reachable states). -/
theorem dBound_of_reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    DBound s := by
  induction h with
  | init => intro q x hx; simp [S3.init] at hx
  | step _ hs ih => exact kstep_dBound hs ih

/-- Shape of the `internal` authority of every stack (DS-v1, non-normative; §76.2: own mode
`Modify`; §76.3: its footprint contains the footprint of the storage, the cells of the stack; §42:
modes and footprints never change): it exists, has own mode `Modify` and covers every cell. -/
def StackShape (D : DState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), D.stacks[i]? = some st →
    ∃ y : Authority, D.kern.A[st.internal]? = some y ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧
    ∀ c ∈ st.cells, c ∈ y.footprint

/-- The kernel part of a library step keeps every authority (DS-v1, non-normative; §42, `AKeep`;
Part XIV: the steps of `push`, `rewind`, `grow` are kernel steps). -/
theorem DStep.akeep {k : K} {D D' : DState} (h : DStep k D D') : AKeep D.kern D'.kern := by
  cases h with
  | kernel hk => exact kstep_akeep hk
  | newStack hs =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact akeep_append (List.append_nil _).symm
  | push hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ _ _ hsp hst => exact (kstep_akeep (.split hsp)).trans (kstep_akeep (k := k) (.store hst))
  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok _ => exact akeep_append (List.append_nil _).symm
  | rewind hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ _ _ hsp hrl =>
      exact (kstep_akeep (.split hsp)).trans (kstep_akeep (k := k) (.release hrl))
  | grow hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ _ _ hrl _ _ hsp hst =>
      exact ((kstep_akeep (k := k) (.release hrl)).trans (kstep_akeep (.split hsp))).trans
        (kstep_akeep (k := k) (.store hst))

/-- `StackShape` is kept when the authorities are kept and each stack keeps its `internal` and
its cells (DS-v1, non-normative; §42, §46). -/
theorem stackShape_keep {D D' : DState} (hA : AKeep D.kern D'.kern) (hw : StackShape D)
    (hs : ∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), D'.stacks[i]? = some st' →
      ∃ st : Stack, D.stacks[i]? = some st ∧ st'.internal = st.internal ∧ st'.cells = st.cells) :
    StackShape D' := by
  intro i st' h
  obtain ⟨st, hst, hi, hc⟩ := hs i st' h
  obtain ⟨y, hy, hm, hf⟩ := hw i st hst
  obtain ⟨y', hy', hm', hf', -⟩ := hA _ y hy
  exact ⟨y', hi ▸ hy', hm'.trans hm, fun c hc' => hf' ▸ hf c (hc ▸ hc')⟩

/-- Replacing stack `j` by a stack with the same `internal` and cells (DS-v1, non-normative; §46
metadata updates of `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow`). -/
theorem set_keeps {l : List Stack} {j : Nat} {st st₀ : Stack} (hst : l[j]? = some st₀)
    (hi : st.internal = st₀.internal) (hc : st.cells = st₀.cells) :
    ∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), (l.set j st)[i]? = some st' →
      ∃ st'' : Stack, l[i]? = some st'' ∧ st'.internal = st''.internal ∧
        st'.cells = st''.cells := by
  intro i st' h
  rcases getElem?_set_cases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
  · exact ⟨st₀, hst, hi, hc⟩
  · exact ⟨st', h, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- Every library step keeps `StackShape` (DS-v1, non-normative; §76.2, §76.3 at `newStack`,
§42 afterwards). -/
theorem DStep.stackShape {k : K} {D D' : DState} (h : DStep k D D') (hw : StackShape D) :
    StackShape D' := by
  have hA := h.akeep
  cases h with
  | kernel => exact stackShape_keep hA hw fun i st' h => ⟨st', h, rfl, rfl⟩
  | @newStack _ _ _ int hs =>
    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
    intro i st' h
    rcases getElem?_append_single h with h | rfl
    · exact hw i st' h
    · have hi := hp.base.internalAuth
      cases hy : D.kern.A[int]? with
      | none => rw [hy] at hi; exact hi.elim
      | some y =>
        rw [hy] at hi
        refine ⟨y, hy, hi.2, fun c hc => ?_⟩
        have := hp.base.fpSup c hc; simpa [S3.afp, hy] using this
  | push hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
  | rewind hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
  | grow hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)

/-- Every library-reachable state satisfies `StackShape` (DS-v1, non-normative; §47: no stack
initially; §76.2, §76.3, §42). -/
theorem DReach.stackShape {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
    StackShape D := by
  induction h with
  | init => intro i st h; simp [DState.init] at h
  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.stackShape ih

/-- The authority added by `split` of `src` on one region can be released at once (support for
DS-v1, non-normative, `rewind`; §62): it is active, derived, held by the current frame (§62.1,
§62.2), has no descendant (§62.3: origins precede, §42) and, under `DBound`, anchors no place
(§62.3, §62.4). -/
theorem release_after_split {s : S3} {src : Nat} {R : List Nat} (hb : DBound s) :
    ReleasePre (splitEff s src [R]) s.A.length := by
  have hy₀ := split_block s src R
  refine ⟨⟨_, hy₀, rfl⟩, by rw [hy₀]; simp [OptP], by rw [hy₀]; exact rfl,
    fun j hj hn => ?_, fun q _ _ hx => absurd (hb q _ hx) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)⟩
  have := chain_lt hn
  have := List.mem_range.1 hj; simp [splitEff] at this; omega

/-- `rewind_ok_iff` (DS-v1, non-normative: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an
active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to
available"; §36; §61.1, §61.3, §62 through Part XIV). On a library-reachable state (`DReach`, a
state invariant), for an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` exactly when `m` is a live mark of the
stack (DS-v1), the administrative right of §36 holds (`AdminRight`), and no active authority
derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m` (DS-v1). The model has no explicit check of the
last condition: it is the effective `Modify` of `internal` required by `split` (§61.1, with the
effective mode of §43). The other checks of `split` and `release` never reject there: `internal`
has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`, §76.2, §76.3), and anchors name
existing authorities (`dBound_of_reachable`). DS-v1 does not list §36: on the reachable state of
`Witness.reading_rewind_right` every DS-v1 condition for success holds and §36 rejects (the §61.1
check of `split` fails there too). -/
theorem rewind_ok_iff {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (hr : DReach k statics D)
    {j : Nat} {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {m : Mark} :
    (∃ D', RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) ↔
      LiveMark j st m ∧ AdminRight D.kern st ∧
        ∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), D.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
          st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x → l ∈ y.footprint → l ∉ above st m := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨D', h⟩
    cases h with
    | ok h hm ha hsp =>
      rw [hst] at h; cases h
      have hp := (Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp).1
      exact ⟨hm, ha, fun x l y hy ya hx hly hl =>
        no_desc_of_modify hy ya hly hx (hp.modifyOn _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hm, ha, hno⟩
    obtain ⟨yi, hyi, hmi, hci⟩ := hr.stackShape j st hst
    have yia : yi.active = true := by
      obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := ha.1; rw [hyi] at hy; cases hy; exact ya
    have hab : ∀ l ∈ above st m, l ∈ yi.footprint :=
      fun l hl => hci l (List.mem_of_mem_drop (List.mem_of_mem_take hl))
    have hmod : ∀ l ∈ above st m, effective D.kern st.internal l = some .modify := by
      intro l hl
      have hd : descModes D.kern st.internal l = [] := by
        apply nil_of_forall_not_mem; intro e he
        obtain ⟨x, y, hy, ya, hly, hx, -⟩ := mem_descModes.1 he
        exact hno x l y hy ya hx hly hl
      rw [effective_eq hyi yia (hab l hl), hd]; simp [effOf, hmi]
    have hex : D.kern.ExercisableAt st.internal .modify := by
      have hmr := ha.2
      simp only [MetaRight, arenaValue, Stack.entry, hyi] at hmr
      cases hv : yi.holder with
      | frame f => rw [hv] at hmr; exact hmr.elim
      | place v =>
        rw [hv] at hmr
        obtain ⟨b, -, hb, hall⟩ := hmr
        exact .held hyi yia (.inr hmi) hv hb hall
    have hsp : SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [above st m] := by
      refine ⟨ha.1, hex, fun r hr p hp => ?_, fun r hr p hp => ?_, List.pairwise_singleton _ _,
        fun r hr p hp x _ hd => ?_⟩
      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr] at hp; exact hmod p hp
      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr] at hp
        exact ⟨by simp only [S3.afp, hyi]; exact hab p hp, by rw [hmod p hp]; simp⟩
      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr] at hp
        unfold DistribExcl at hd
        cases hx : D.kern.A[x]? with
        | none => rw [hx] at hd; exact hd
        | some y =>
          rw [hx] at hd; obtain ⟨ya, hanc, hpy, -⟩ := hd; exact hno x p y hx ya hanc hpy hp
    exact ⟨_, .ok hst hm ha (.ok hsp)
      (.ok (release_after_split (dBound_of_reachable hr.reachable)))⟩

/-! ## Marks are never reused (`mark_no_aba`) -/

/-- Well-formed marks (DS-v1, non-normative, "marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark
identifier"; support; library metadata, §38): the live marks of stack `i` are pairwise distinct,
name stack `i`, and have identifiers already given out. -/
def MarksWF (D : DState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), D.stacks[i]? = some st →
    st.marks.Nodup ∧ ∀ m ∈ st.marks, m.stack = i ∧ m.id < D.fresh

435:For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.
560:The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.
658:`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.
895:An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.
916:1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
935:1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.

## 35. Transfer and Pinning

Value transfer is prohibited when it would invalidate an active derived access. A legal transfer does not turn a second-class authority into a freely copyable persistent reference and must preserve its validity chain and anchor dependencies.

Transferring a value never physically moves storage owned by it. Moving an **in-place** leaf is rejected when that leaf is pinned; pinning only the owned storage does not prohibit transfer of the owning value. Detailed constraints belong to `transfer` (O4), `Pinned`, and pinning invariant I5.

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

theorem d7_reach : DReach K0 wst d7 := by
  have r1 : DReach K0 wst d1 := .step .init (.kernel (.derive (.ok (by decide))))
  have r2 : DReach K0 wst d2 := .step r1 (.kernel (.store (.ok (by decide))))
  have r3 : DReach K0 wst d3 := .step r2 (.newStack (others := []) (.ok (by decide)))
  have r4 : DReach K0 wst d4 := .step r3 (.mark (.ok (st := st3) (by decide)))
  have r5 : DReach K0 wst d5 := .step r4
    (.push (.ok (st := st4) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide))
      (.ok (by decide))))
  have r6 : DReach K0 wst d6 := .step r5 (.mark (.ok (st := st5) (by decide)))
  exact .step r6
    (.push (.ok (st := st6) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide))
      (.ok (by decide))))

/-- The run up to the rewind is library-reachable (DS-v1; §62, Part XIV derived `reset`, §78). -/
theorem d9_reach : DReach K0 wst d9 :=
  .step (.step d7_reach (.kernel (.release (.ok (by decide)))))
    (.rewind (.ok (st := st7) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide))
      (.ok (by decide))))

/-- **Non-vacuity of the DS-v1 operations** (§58 outcomes). In `d7`, `rewind ⟨0, 1, 1⟩` is
rejected: block 6, derived from `internal` 4, covers cell 3 above the mark
(`rewind_rejects_live_above`); `grow` of block 5, which is not at the top, fails (DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). After the program releases 6, `rewind ⟨0, 1, 1⟩` is `ok`: the top returns to 1,
the older mark stays; the removed mark then fails (`mark_no_aba`). `grow` of block 5 by one cell
is then `ok` in place: block `⟨0, 2, 8, 4⟩`, whose authority 8 covers the cells 2 and 3. -/
theorem run_ok :
    DReach K0 wst d10 ∧
    RewindStep K0 0 m1 d7 .reject ∧ GrowStep K0 0 5 1 d7 .fail ∧
    d9.stacks = [⟨1, 4, [2, 3], 1, [x5], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩]⟩] ∧ RewindStep K0 0 m1 d9 .fail ∧
    d10.stacks = [⟨1, 4, [2, 3], 2, [⟨0, 2, 8, 4⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩]⟩] ∧ d10.kern.afp 8 = [2, 3] := by
  have r10 : DReach K0 wst d10 := .step d9_reach
    (.grow (.ok (st := st9) (x := x5) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide))
      (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))))
  have hrej := (rewind_rejects_live_above (k := K0) (D := d7) (j := 0) (st := st7) (m := m1)
    (x := 6) (l := 3) (y := ⟨.modify, some 4, [3], .place 5, true⟩) (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide) rfl (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)).1
  have hfail : GrowStep K0 0 5 1 d7 .fail :=
    .fail (st := st7) (x := x5) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (by decide)
      (by decide)
  exact ⟨r10, hrej, hfail, by decide, (rewind_dead_fails (st := st9) (by decide) (by decide)).1,
    by decide, by decide⟩

/-! ### Readings with a changed verdict (DS-v1)

Each theorem below shows, on a library-reachable state, a program whose verdict or arrival state
depends on a reading of DS-v1 recorded in the readings: the verdict or arrival state of the reading
formalized here, and the facts that make the other reading give another one. -/

/-- `release(5)` by the program, after the rewind (§62; DS-v1 non-vacuity). -/
def d11 : DState := ⟨releaseEff d9.kern 5, d9.stacks, d9.fresh⟩
/-- `derive(4, [3], Modify)` by the program: authority 8 on cell 3, above the current top (§60;
DS-v1 reading of "above"). -/
def d12 : DState := ⟨deriveEff d11.kern 4 [3] .modify, d11.stacks, d11.fresh⟩
/-- The first mark (DS-v1, §58). -/
def m0 : Mark := ⟨0, 0, 0⟩
/-- A callee frame with no parameter and no local, entered after the rewind (§72; DS-v1 reading
of the order of `fail` and the right of §36). -/
def d13 : DState := ⟨enterEff d9.kern [] [], d9.stacks, d9.fresh⟩

/-- **Reading of "a cell above m"** (DS-v1, §46). In `d12`, authority 8, active and derived from
`internal` 4, covers cell 3, at a position above the top of mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` but above the current
top too, hence not among the cells `rewind` returns (`above`): `rewind ⟨0, 0, 0⟩` is `ok`. Under the
reading "any cell at a position at or above the top of `m`", it is rejected. -/
theorem reading_above :
    DReach K0 wst d12 ∧ d12.kern.A[8]? = some ⟨.modify, some 4, [3], .frame 0, true⟩ ∧
    st9.internal ∈ d12.kern.ancs 8 ∧ 3 ∈ st9.cells.drop m0.top ∧ 3 ∉ above st9 m0 ∧
    ∃ D', RewindStep K0 0 m0 d12 (.ok D') := by
  have r11 : DReach K0 wst d11 := .step d9_reach (.kernel (.release (.ok (by decide))))
  have r12 : DReach K0 wst d12 := .step r11 (.kernel (.derive (.ok (by decide))))
  exact ⟨r12, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    ⟨_, .ok (st := st9) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))⟩⟩

/-- **Readings of the order of checks and of `extra = 0`** (DS-v1, §58, §36). (1) In `d13`, a callee
with no right on the stack value (`¬ AdminRight`) rewinds to the removed mark `⟨0, 1, 1⟩`: the
outcome is `fail` (dead mark checked first); with the right of §36 checked first it is `reject`.
(2) In `d9`, `grow(0, 5, 0)` is rejected (`extra = 0`), while the sequence `release`, static checks,
in-place check, `split`, `store` of the same region would be `ok`. (3) In `d3`, `push(0, 3, 4)` asks
for more cells than the storage has: `fail` (availability), although the requested cells are not all
in the storage. -/
theorem reading_order :
    DReach K0 wst d13 ∧ ¬ AdminRight d13.kern st9 ∧ RewindStep K0 0 m1 d13 .fail ∧
    GrowStep K0 0 5 0 d9 .reject ∧
    ReleaseStep 5 d9.kern (.ok (releaseEff d9.kern 5)) ∧
    IssueStatic (releaseEff d9.kern 5) st9.entry (cellsOf st9 x5.base (x5.size + 0)) x5.dst ∧
    InPlace st9 x5 0 ∧
    SplitStep K0 st9.internal [cellsOf st9 x5.base (x5.size + 0)] (releaseEff d9.kern 5)
      (.ok (splitEff (releaseEff d9.kern 5) st9.internal [cellsOf st9 x5.base (x5.size + 0)])) ∧
    StoreStep (releaseEff d9.kern 5).A.length x5.dst
      (splitEff (releaseEff d9.kern 5) st9.internal [cellsOf st9 x5.base (x5.size + 0)])
      (.ok (storeEff (splitEff (releaseEff d9.kern 5) st9.internal
        [cellsOf st9 x5.base (x5.size + 0)]) (releaseEff d9.kern 5).A.length x5.dst)) ∧
    PushStep K0 0 3 4 d3 .fail := by
  have r13 : DReach K0 wst d13 := .step d9_reach (.kernel (.enter (.ok (by decide))))
  exact ⟨r13, by decide, .dead (st := st9) (by decide) (by decide),
    .noExtra (st := st9) (x := x5) (by decide) (by decide) rfl, .ok (by decide), by decide,
    by decide, .ok (by decide), .ok (by decide),
    .fail (st := st3) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)⟩

frame with no right on the stack value 0 (no `AdminRight`, no `Observe` right, no valid
`writeShared` through any authority, §68) marks stack 0: `ok`, a mark appended to the metadata.
Under the reading of §36 ¶1 (metadata modified "to the extent permitted by the applicable
rights"), these facts give `reject`. -/
theorem reading_mark :
    DReach K0 wst d13 ∧ d13.stacks[0]? = some st9 ∧ ¬ AdminRight d13.kern st9 ∧
    ¬ HasRight d13.kern .observe 0 ∧
    (∀ a ∈ List.range d13.kern.A.length, ¬ WriteSharedPre K0 d13.kern a (footprint d13.kern.P 0)) ∧
    MarkStep 0 d13 (.ok ⟨d13.kern, d13.stacks.set 0 (markMeta 0 st9 d13.fresh), d13.fresh + 1⟩) :=
  ⟨reading_order.1, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩

5, moves from place 4 to place 5, and place 4 becomes `Moved` (§63; DS-v1 reading of the `grow`
destination). -/
def d14 : DState := ⟨transferEff d5.kern 4 5, d5.stacks, d5.fresh⟩

/-- The kernel state of `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d14` after `release(5)` and `split(4, [[2, 3]])`
(§62, §61; DS-v1 reading of the `grow` destination). -/
def s14 : S3 :=
  splitEff (releaseEff d14.kern 5) st5.internal [cellsOf st5 x5.base (x5.size + 1)]

/-- `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d14`: `release(5)`, `split(4, [[2, 3]])`, `store(6, 4)` into the recorded
destination 4 (DS-v1, Part XIV, §77). -/
def d15 : DState :=
  ⟨storeEff s14 (releaseEff d14.kern 5).A.length x5.dst,
    d14.stacks.set 0 (growMeta st5 x5 1 (releaseEff d14.kern 5).A.length), d14.fresh⟩

/-- **Reading of the `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst`** (DS-v1, non-normative; §63, §65,
§77). In `d14`, the block value of block 5, recorded with destination 4, was transferred to place 5,
which now holds authority 5, and place 4 is `Moved`. `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new
block authority 6 into the moved-from place 4, which becomes `Init`. Under the reading "the current
holder of `b`", the static checks of the derived issue and `store` into place 5 are `ok` on the same
released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5: another arrival state. -/
theorem reading_grow_dst :
    DReach K0 wst d14 ∧ d14.stacks[0]? = some st5 ∧ st5.block 5 = some x5 ∧ x5.dst = 4 ∧
    d14.kern.A[5]?.map (·.holder) = some (.place 5) ∧ d14.kern.I 4 = .moved ∧
    GrowStep K0 0 5 1 d14 (.ok d15) ∧
    d15.kern.A[d14.kern.A.length]?.map (·.holder) = some (.place 4) ∧ d15.kern.I 4 = .init ∧
    IssueStatic (releaseEff d14.kern 5) st5.entry (cellsOf st5 x5.base (x5.size + 1)) 5 ∧
    StoreStep (releaseEff d14.kern 5).A.length 5 s14
      (.ok (storeEff s14 (releaseEff d14.kern 5).A.length 5)) ∧
    (storeEff s14 (releaseEff d14.kern 5).A.length 5).A[d14.kern.A.length]?.map (·.holder) =
      some (.place 5) := by

  have r2 : DReach K0 wst d2 := .step r1 (.kernel (.store (.ok (by decide))))
  have r3 : DReach K0 wst d3 := .step r2 (.newStack (others := []) (.ok (by decide)))

    (.push (.ok (st := st4) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide))
      (.ok (by decide))))

    by decide,
    .ok (st := st5) (x := x5) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (by decide)
      (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (.ok (by decide)),
    by decide, by decide, by decide, .ok (by decide), by decide⟩

/-- Statics of the `newStack` reading (§47; DS-v1 reading of §76.5): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owned by
frame 0, is the stack value; leaf 1, owned by static 0, is the storage, whose root authority 1 is
held by place 0. -/
def wsu : Statics := [((none, none, 0), false), ((none, some 0, 0), false)]

/-- **Reading of the `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies** (DS-v1, non-normative; §76.1–§76.3,
§76.5, §56). In the initial state of `wsu`, `newStack(1, 1)` is rejected: the stack value 0 holding
`internal` 1 is `Uninit` (§76.5). Every other precondition holds: storage 1 usable under
exercisable `Modify` (§76.1); `internal` 1 active, of own mode `Modify`, exercisable (§76.2), held
by place 0 with the footprint of the storage (§76.3); the guard of §56. Under the reading that
drops §76.5 for a stack, the outcome is `ok`. -/
theorem reading_newStack :
    DReach K0 wsu (DState.init wsu) ∧ NewStackStep [] 1 1 (DState.init wsu) .reject ∧
    (DState.init wsu).kern.A[1]? = some ⟨.modify, none, [1], .place 0, true⟩ ∧
    (DState.init wsu).kern.I 0 = .uninit ∧ ¬ LeavesInit (DState.init wsu).kern (.place 0) ∧
    (DState.init wsu).kern.Usable 1 ∧ HasRight (DState.init wsu).kern .modify 1 ∧
    (DState.init wsu).kern.ExercisableAt 1 .modify ∧
    (∀ l ∈ (DState.init wsu).kern.afp 1, l ∈ footprint (DState.init wsu).kern.P 1) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint (DState.init wsu).kern.P 1, l ∈ (DState.init wsu).kern.afp 1) ∧
    Guard56 [stackInternals (DState.init wsu).kern (DState.init wsu).stacks] 1 :=
  ⟨.init, .reject (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-- A callee frame with no parameter and no local, entered after the program's `release(5)` that
follows the rewind (§72; DS-v1, non-normative: reading of the reasons for which `rewind`
rejects). -/

§61.1). In `d16`, mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` is live for stack 0 and no active authority derived from
`internal` 4 covers the cell 2 above it (blocks 5, 6 and 7 are released): every condition DS-v1
lists for the `ok` case holds. The callee has no right on the stack value (`¬ AdminRight`, §36), so
`rewind ⟨0, 0, 0⟩` is `reject` and never `ok` (`rewind_ok_iff`); `split` of `internal` alone would
reject too (`internal` is not exercisable at `Modify`, §61.1). Under the reading that DS-v1 lists
every reason to reject, the outcome is `ok`. -/
theorem reading_rewind_right :
    DReach K0 wst d16 ∧ d16.stacks[0]? = some st9 ∧ LiveMark 0 st9 m0 ∧
    (∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), d16.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
      st9.internal ∈ d16.kern.ancs x → l ∈ y.footprint → l ∉ above st9 m0) ∧
    ¬ AdminRight d16.kern st9 ∧ ¬ d16.kern.ExercisableAt st9.internal .modify ∧
    RewindStep K0 0 m0 d16 .reject ∧ ¬ ∃ D', RewindStep K0 0 m0 d16 (.ok D') := by
  have r16 : DReach K0 wst d16 :=
    .step (.step d9_reach (.kernel (.release (.ok (by decide)))))
      (.kernel (.enter (.ok (by decide))))
  have hst : d16.stacks[0]? = some st9 := by decide
  have hna : ¬ AdminRight d16.kern st9 := by decide
  have hb : ∀ x ∈ List.range d16.kern.A.length, OptP (d16.kern.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true →
      st9.internal ∈ d16.kern.ancs x → ∀ l ∈ above st9 m0, l ∉ y.footprint) True := by decide
  refine ⟨r16, hst, by decide, fun x l y hy ya hx hly hl => ?_, hna, by decide,
    .static hst (by decide) hna, fun h => hna ((rewind_ok_iff r16 hst).1 h).2.1⟩
  have := hb x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy))
  rw [hy] at this

end Witness

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow
## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

8:Cette section appartient à la **Spec 1 — Modèle mémoire** ; elle ne constitue pas à elle seule le document final de la Spec 1. Les noms des opérations sont des noms sémantiques provisoires, et non une syntaxe ERN adoptée. La spécification écrite prévaut sur ses modèles Lean ; la validation doit vérifier la cohérence de la spécification écrite et du registre de reconstruction, et non donner au modèle exploratoire une autorité normative.
434:Les théorèmes exploratoires `init_only_by_writes` (un pas) et `init_statics` (état initial) étayent cette garantie. La reconstruction de référence devra expliciter l'induction correspondante sur `Reachable` et la correspondance entre la relation générique `Step` et ses constructeurs, sans présumer qu'elles sont déjà énoncées dans le module exploratoire.
555:Les obligations R1, R2, le reste de R4 et R6 n'ont **pas** été closes par le jalon 1. La reconstruction de référence pourra utiliser la formalisation exploratoire, mais elle ne peut pas remplacer le texte normatif par des hypothèses ajoutées dans Lean.
577:| Corpus adversariaux MM3-H et MM23-H | **Jalon 3 achevé**, sous les écarts connus explicités dans son rapport ; MM2-H doit encore être exécuté contre la reconstruction de référence. Les cas concurrents dépendants sont à rouvrir après la Spec 2. |
583:Les jalons 1–3 sont clos dans les limites documentées de leurs rapports. La présente v0.4 incorpore seulement les décisions expressément retenues à leur issue. Le modèle exploratoire doit être reconstruit après validation du document normatif assemblé ; cette reconstruction doit vérifier les écarts et obligations des registres, sans correction silencieuse du texte. La clôture des jalons ne vaut pas gel de la Spec 1 complète.
622:La forme forte de F6 (`call_protects_params_safe`) est réfutée par des états atteints, et non remplacée par un théorème silencieusement affaibli. L'absence de `NoLock` est compatible avec les invariants prouvés, mais ne garantit pas l'absence d'autorités détenues devenues inexerçables. Sans `DDSound`, le témoin `split_unsound_without_DD` réfute l'exclusivité globale. Hors de `WF3`, certains transferts peuvent faire tomber `Inv3` : ces états ne sont pas atteints dans le cadre du théorème principal. Le jalon 1 n'a pas encore de théorème autonome reliant tous les constructeurs `Reachable` à `Step` ni de théorème historique global sur chaque feuille `Init` atteinte : ces deux lemmes sont prévus pour la reconstruction de référence.
647:**Historique du corpus :** l’inventaire initial comptait `MM2-H` (17), `MM3-H` (43) et `MM23-H` (14). Les corpus MM3-H et MM23-H ont été enrichis et exécutés au jalon 3 (`J3_v0.1.md`). Les verdicts actualisés, les variantes, les cas inter-spécifications et les écarts connus sont consignés dans les annexes du document assemblé. **MM2-H doit être exécuté contre la reconstruction de référence** ; sa présence dans le dossier ne vaut pas preuve de conformité. Les cas concurrents requérant les règles de synchronisation seront alors identifiés comme dépendants de la Spec 2.
713:L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.
736:# Annexe F — Registre de reconstruction de référence (non normatif)
738:La reconstruction de référence doit repartir du texte **validé**, et non des approximations du brouillon. Les éléments suivants ne sont pas tous prouvés à ce stade :
711:`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

  unfold ContentAnchorOK OptP at hc; rw [hy] at hc
  obtain ⟨hnh, -, hl⟩ := hc
  exact ⟨y, by rw [endUseEff, EndFree.cleanup_get, EndFree.endUseS_get, hy]; simp [hnh, hl], ya⟩

/-- The end of the content preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §69; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3), under
`WF3` (§49) and `I1` (§50): an active authority on a leaf of a place that stops being usable is
derived, and blocked by §69.2 on dying storage, or a root, held by the owner of the root place of
the leaf (`rootHeldConv_active`), which stays usable. -/
theorem contentEnd_noDangling {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)
    (h1 : I1 s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) (hw' : WF3 (endUseEff s q)) :
    NoDangling (endUseEff s q) := by
  have hU := EndFree.cleanup_usable (endUseS s q)
  intro j z hz za q' hq l hl hlz
  obtain ⟨hz₀, hnh, hlive⟩ := EndFree.endUse_active hz za
  by_cases hq₀ : ¬ s.Usable q'
  · exact hnd j z hz₀ za q' hq₀ l hl hlz
  replace hq₀ := Decidable.of_not_not hq₀
  obtain ⟨-, hleaf, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  have hl₀ : s.Usable l := usable_of_partOf hw (l + 1) l q' (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlq hq₀
  have hl₁ : ¬ (endUseS s q).Usable l := fun hu => hq (usable_of_part hw' hlq ((hU l).2 hu))
  cases hzo : z.origin with
  | some o =>
    have hacc := hpre.dying j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz₀))
    unfold DyingAccessOK OptP at hacc; rw [hz₀] at hacc
    rcases hacc za (by rw [hzo]; simp) ⟨l, hlz, hleaf, hl₀, hl₁⟩ with e | e
    · exact hnh e
    · exact e hlive
  | none =>
    obtain ⟨-, -, r, -, -, -, hr, hlr, -⟩ := hw.rootChain j z l hz₀ hlz hleaf
    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hh⟩ := rootHeldConv_active hw h1 hnd j z l r hz₀ za hzo hlz hr hlr
    have hnown : ¬ OwnedIn s.P q r := fun hown => by
      cases hown with
      | @direct _ o _ hpl ho hpart =>
        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
        rw [hh, e] at hnh; exact hnh hpart
      | @step _ o _ hpl ho hown' =>
        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
        rw [hh, e] at hlive
        have := EndFree.dead_false hlive
        simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at this
        exact this.2 hown'
    have hd : (endUseS s q).dead r = false := by
      simp only [endUseS, ← hw.deadOf hlr, EndFree.dead_false hl₀, Bool.false_or,
        decide_eq_false_iff_not]
      exact hnown
    have hr₁ : (endUseS s q).Usable r := EndFree.usable_of_owner hpr hd (hh ▸ hlive)
    exact hl₁ ((hU l).1 (usable_of_partOf hw' (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlr ((hU r).2 hr₁)))

/-- The end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` preserves the kernel invariant
`KInv` (§57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la correspondance des effets et la préservation des
invariants sous ce droit constituent une obligation explicite de reconstruction"; §69 effect); the auxiliary `KAux` is preserved by
`contentEnd_preserves_kAux`. -/
theorem contentEnd_preserves {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hk : KInv s)
    (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) : KInv (endUseEff s q) := by
  have hw := hk.1
  refine EndFree.releases_preserve hk (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl rfl rfl
    (fun q h => by simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff] at h; exact h.1)
    (fun q' pl r hq hp => ?_) (fun q' _ x hx => ?_) (contentEnd_anchors hk.2.1.1.2.2.1 hpre)
    (fun r n z pr _ hur hz _ _ hpr hzh _ => ?_)
    (contentEnd_noDangling hw hk.2.1.2.2 hk.2.1.1.1 hpre)
  · obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, hd⟩ := hw.places q' pl r hq hp
    simp only [endUseS, hd, decide_eq_decide.2 (EndFree.ownedIn_parent hw hq hp)]
  · simp only [endUseS] at hx; split at hx
    · simp at hx
    · exact hx
  · have hnh : ¬ heldIn s.P q z.holder := fun hh => by
      have hd := EndFree.dead_false hur
      simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at hd
      rw [hzh] at hh
      cases ho : pr.owner with
      | frame f => rw [ho] at hh; exact hh
      | place o => rw [ho] at hh; exact hd.2 (.direct hpr ho hh)
    rw [EndFree.endUseS_get, hz]; simp [hnh]

/-- The end of the content of a slot place `q` preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40,
§49.7; not a clause of §57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69 effect: places are unchanged and
authorities are only released). -/
theorem contentEnd_preserves_kAux {s : S3} {q : Nat} (ha : KAux s) : KAux (endUseEff s q) :=
  EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux ha (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl

/-! ## Kernel side of the pool operations (§57, §58; HandlePool v0.4 annex) -/

/-- Sequences of kernel steps compose (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem KSeq.trans {k : K} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : S3} (h₁ : KSeq k s₁ s₂) (h₂ : KSeq k s₂ s₃) :
      · have := chain_lt h'; omega
    rw [hnil, hmy]; rfl
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := hok.slotLeaf q hq
  exact ⟨Arena.usable_of_covered hnd hy ya (hcov l hl) hl,
    ⟨pl.internal, List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy), hex,
      fun l hl => by rw [heff l hl]; exact Arena.allows_some_modify _⟩⟩

/-- An accepted `freeSlot` preserves the kernel invariant `KInv` (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3:
"la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une
obligation explicite de reconstruction"); the auxiliary
`KAux` is preserved by `freeSlot_preserves_kAux`. -/
theorem freeSlot_preserves {k : K} {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} (hk : KInv L.kern)
    (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KInv L'.kern := by
  obtain ⟨pl, sl, -, -, -, -, hpre, he, -⟩ := pool_freeSlot_ends_content hst
  rw [he]; exact contentEnd_preserves hk hpre

/-- An accepted `freeSlot` preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40, §49.7; not a clause
of §57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69 effect). -/
theorem freeSlot_preserves_kAux {k : K} {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle}
    (ha : KAux L.kern) (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KAux L'.kern := by
  obtain ⟨pl, sl, -, -, -, -, -, he, -⟩ := pool_freeSlot_ends_content hst
  rw [he]; exact contentEnd_preserves_kAux ha

  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ hs ih => exact xreach_pstep ih (hX _ ih) hs

/-- `KInv` (§57) together with the auxiliary `KAux` (§40, §49.7; not a clause of §57) holds on
every state reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents, when it holds initially and every
kernel step O1–O16 preserves it (`contentEnd_preserves` and `contentEnd_preserves_kAux` cover the
ends of slot contents; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem xreach_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (h0 : KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics))
    (hK : ∀ s s', KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∧ KAux s') {s : S3}
    (h : XReach k statics s) : KInv s ∧ KAux s := by
  induction h with

"""Recompute the summary counts of table-final.md (sections A, B, C) and of blocking-report.md
(section 1 rows by class, section 7 questions). Usage: counts.py TABLE REPORT"""
import re, sys, collections, json
T = open(sys.argv[1]).read().split('\n'); R = open(sys.argv[2]).read().split('\n')
def sec(lines, start, stop):
    a = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith(start)); b = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if i > a and l.startswith(stop))
    return lines[a:b]
def status(l):
    m = re.search(r'\| \*\*([^*]+)\*\*', l); return m.group(1)
A = [l for l in sec(T, '## A.', '## B.') if l.startswith('| §')]
B = [l for l in sec(T, '## B.', '## C.') if re.match(r'\| (O\d|R\.)', l)]
ca = collections.Counter(status(l) for l in A); cb = collections.Counter(status(l) for l in B)
print('A rows', len(A), dict(ca))
print('A open:', [l.split(' | ')[0][2:] for l in A if status(l).startswith('open')])
print('A conditional:', [l.split(' | ')[0][2:] for l in A if status(l) == 'conditional'])
print('B rows', len(B), dict(cb))
for k in cb: print('  ', k, [l.split(' ')[1] for l in B if status(l) == k])
C = [l for l in sec(T, '## C.', '## D.') if l.startswith('- §')]
print('C rows', len(C))
rows = [l for l in R if re.match(r'\| B\d+ \|', l)]
def cls(l):
    c = l.split(' | ')[3]
    if c.startswith('module defect'): return 'module defect'
    if c.startswith('case defect'): return 'case defect'
    if c.startswith('specification defect (contract'): return 'specification defect (contract, non-normative)'
    if c.startswith('specification defect'): return 'specification defect (spec v0)'
    return '?' + c
cr = collections.Counter(cls(l) for l in rows)
print('report section 1 rows', len(rows), dict(cr))
for k in cr: print('  ', k, [l.split(' | ')[0][2:] for l in rows if cls(l) == k])
Q = [l for l in R if re.match(r'\*\*Q\d+\.', l)]
print('questions', len(Q), [re.match(r'\*\*(Q\d+)', l).group(1) for l in Q])

## 7. Questions for arbitration

Each question gives the passage, the readings, and, where one is recorded, a program whose verdict changes, with its witness. Q15, Q16 and Q20 have none. The policy readings (`R/policy.md`) and every entry of `R/readings/*.md` are also submitted (Q23).

**Q1. §63 versus §49.8 and §57 (B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B8, B10).**
- Passages: §57, "On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:", followed by WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan (display formula). §49 item 8, "every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place". §58, "An `ok` transition must … preserve the relevant invariants". §63 lists preconditions 1–8, and none requires the destination to remain usable.
- Readings:
  - (a) §63 as written, so §57 is false (current model);
  - (b) add to §63 "destination usable in the resulting state" (the draft clause), which makes `reachableDU_kinv` §57 for statics satisfying `StaticsOK`; §57 also needs the §47 repair (Q8, B36) (`R/reports/kernel-main.md` P-M1);
  - (c) another repair chosen by the spec owner.
- Program: statics `src` (leaf 0, `Init`) and `prov` (leaf 1, `Init`); `alloc(prov, owner 0)` makes place 2; `alloc(prov, owner 2)` makes place 3; then `transfer(0, 3)`. Under (a) the transfer is `ok`, places 2 and 3 own each other and §49.8 fails. Under (b) it is `reject`.
- Witnesses: `Access.transfer_breaks_kinv` (Transfer.lean:781), `Access.reachable_kinv_false` (Main.lean:685), `Access.transfer_kinv_iff` (Main.lean:465).

**Q2. §76.6 (B33).**
- Passage: "Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected arena invariants."
606:**Q11. DataStack readings (contract DS-v1, non-normative; B29, B30).**
675:**Q23. All recorded readings, submitted as the policy requires.**
**Q11. DataStack readings (contract DS-v1, non-normative; B29, B30).**
- Passages: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark", "push and grow use the derived issue", "grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise)".
- (a) DS-R7: `push` without room. `fail` (current) or `reject` (§77.2 static). Program `Corpus.DataStack.DS05`.
- (b) DS-R5: `grow` of a `b` that is no block. `reject` (current) or `fail`. Program `Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`.
- (c) DS-R9: §76.5 applies to `newStack`. `Witness.reading_newStack` (DataStack.lean:1256): `reject` here, `ok` without §76.5.
- (d) DS-R10: `mark` needs no right. `Witness.reading_mark` (:1193): `ok` here, `reject` under §36 ¶1.
- (e) DS-R11: the `grow` destination is the recorded `Blk.dst`. `Witness.reading_grow_dst` (:1222): the arrival holder is place 4 here and place 5 under the alternative.
- (f) DS-R2: the dead or foreign mark gives `fail` before §36 (current), or the right is checked first (`reject`). Program: a callee with no right rewinds to a removed mark (`R/readings/datastack.md` DS-R2, `Witness.reading_order`).
- (g) DS-R12 and DS-R13, the reasons for which `rewind` rejects: Q27 and Q28.

**Q23. All recorded readings, submitted as the policy requires.**
- `R/readings/kernel-defs.md`: B#1–B#47 and SP-A1–SP-A5. Verdict-changing examples:
  - B#1, §43 one authority over all leaves (∃∀): `split(root S, [[f1],[f2]])` then `pin(S)` is `reject` under ∃∀ and `ok` under ∀∃;
  - B#15, §62.3: W4, `split(a, [[]])` then `release(a)` is `reject` or `ok`;
  - B#28, §69.2 qualifier dropped: W3 (`kd_Readings.lean`:28-34), `endUse` through a `Modify` parameter is `reject` or `ok`;
  - B#33, §70.4 scope;
  - B#45, per-leaf pin flags: `pin(S); pin(f1); unpin(f1); transfer(f1, d)` is `ok` or `reject`;
  - SP-A4, the domain of `StaticPinnedBottom`;
  - B#39, provider usability: its recorded consequence "none on states with `NoDangling`" is false (Q24, B46).
- `R/readings/handlepool.md` H-R1–H-R11 (H-R5 is the scope of the exemption).
- `R/readings/datastack.md` DS-R1–DS-R13, including the missing-stack case of DS-R3 (`RewindStep.noStack`, DataStack.lean:218: `reject` here, `fail` if the mark counts as dead or foreign; `R/final5/nostack.lean`).
- `R/readings/arena.md` A-R766.
- `R/readings/machine.md` S1 (§15.3, "required" bytes) and S2 (byte read vs typed read).
- Also to settle: B44 (definitions of the clauses with no checkable content). B43 (DESIGN.md step function vs §20.1 relations) is a DESIGN.md wording question for its owner, not a spec question (note under the table of section 1).


**Q10. §61.4 (B38).**
- Passage: "Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations." Note to §61: "without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1".

/-- Bounded `I1` for one pair (§50). -/
def I1Pair (s : S3) (a b : Nat) : Prop :=
  a ≠ b → OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun x => OptP (s.A[b]?) (fun y => x.active = true → y.active = true →
    (∃ p ∈ x.footprint, p ∈ y.footprint) → a ∉ s.ancs b → b ∉ s.ancs a →
      x.mode = .observe ∧ y.mode = .observe) True) True

/-- Decidability of `I1Pair` (§50). -/

`y` (§51). -/

  OptP y.origin (fun a => OptP (s.A[a]?)
    (fun x => y.mode.le x.mode ∧ ∀ p ∈ y.footprint, p ∈ x.footprint) False) True

  unfold OriginOK; infer_instance

    ?_⟩
  · intro a b x y p hab ha hb xa ya hpx hpy hba hab'
    have h := h1 a (lt_of_getElem? ha) b (lt_of_getElem? hb) hab
    rw [ha] at h; simp only [OptP] at h; rw [hb] at h
    exact h xa ya ⟨p, hpx, hpy⟩ hba hab'
  · intro b y a hb hy

    unfold OriginOK at h

# fix4-ds: B47, when `rewind` is `ok` (DS-v1, non-normative)

Files: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (+281 lines, 0 removed) and `R/readings/datastack.md` (R3 rewritten, DS-R12 added, examples list updated). No commit was made.

## Contract text (brief.md obligation 6, verbatim)

"rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it"

## Result: both (a) and (b), as an exact characterization

`rewind_ok_iff` (DataStack.lean:660) states that on a library-reachable state with an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` iff the three conditions below hold:

```
theorem rewind_ok_iff {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (hr : DReach k statics D)
    {j : Nat} {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {m : Mark} :
    (∃ D', RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) ↔
      LiveMark j st m ∧ AdminRight D.kern st ∧
        ∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), D.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
          st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x → l ∈ y.footprint → l ∉ above st m
```

The hypotheses and conditions, with their sources:
- `DReach`: the library state invariant. It is the only invariant used: no `KInv`, no I3, no `KAux`.
- `LiveMark`: DS-v1, live and own mark.
- `AdminRight`: §36.
- The last conjunct: the DS-v1 condition, in the same form as the hypotheses of `rewind_rejects_live_above`.
- The model has no explicit check for that condition. It is the effective `Modify` of `internal` that `split` requires (§61.1, with the effective mode of §43). §61.3 follows from the same condition.

(b) `Witness.reading_rewind_right` (DataStack.lean:1279) is the counterexample. It is decided on `d16`, a `DReach K0 wst` state, and is recorded as DS-R12:
- In `d16`, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, and no active authority derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2 (`above st9 m0`).
- The current frame is a callee with no right on the stack value, so `¬ AdminRight`.
- `rewind` is `reject` and never `ok`.
- `split` of `internal` alone would also reject there (`¬ ExercisableAt 4 Modify`, §61.1).

The reason for this rejection is §36, which DS-v1 does not list. Under the reading "DS-v1's list is exhaustive" the outcome is `ok`.

## Declarations added (all additions, no existing statement changed)

All added declarations cite a § clause and "DS-v1, non-normative".
- `DBound` (:466): every anchor in `D` is an index of `A` (§44, §42).
- `kstep_dBound` (:471): each of the 16 kernel steps keeps `DBound`.
- `dBound_of_reachable` (:546): `DBound` holds on every kernel-reachable state.
- `StackShape` (:555): `internal` exists, has own mode `Modify` and covers every cell of the stack (§76.2, §76.3, §42).
- `DStep.akeep` (:562): a library step keeps the authorities.
- `stackShape_keep` (:583) and `set_keeps` (:595): helpers for the preservation proof.
- `DStep.stackShape` (:607) and `DReach.stackShape` (:631): `StackShape` is preserved by every library step and holds on every library-reachable state.
- `release_after_split` (:641): the `release` of the fresh `split` authority is accepted under `DBound` (§62).
- `rewind_ok_iff` (:660).
- `Witness.d16` (:1270) and `Witness.reading_rewind_right` (:1279).

## Statement diffs

None. No existing definition, theorem or hypothesis was touched; `git diff` shows 281 insertions and 0 deletions.

## Checks

- `lake build` (whole project) succeeds with no warning and no error.
- The sorry/admit/native_decide/axiom grep prints nothing.
- No `noncomputable` or `set_option` in the file.
- `axcheck.sh Ern.Lib.DataStack` gives 321 constants, 100 theorems, and nothing outside `propext` and `Quot.sound`.
- `#print axioms` gives `[propext, Quot.sound]` for `rewind_ok_iff`, `reading_rewind_right`, `kstep_dBound` and `DReach.stackShape`.

## Not done / open

- It is not proved whether the explicit §36 check (`AdminRight`) ever rejects where the `split` check of §61.1 (`internal` active and exercisable at `Modify`) would accept. Noted in R3.
  - Likely no on `DReach`: `internal` stays held by a place, by §76.3 `heldByPlace` and `AKeep`'s `isPlace` clause, and parameters of §72 must be frame-held. Then `MetaRight` ↔ `ExercisableAt` as in `Arena.metaRight_iff`.
  - Not formalized: the item does not ask for it.
- `RewindStep`'s docstring still points only to `rewind_rejects_live_above`. It was not edited, to keep the diff additive.
- `blocking-report.md` row B47 was not edited: outside my file list.
- `formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean` shows as modified in `git status`. That change is not mine; I did not touch it.

/-- A guarded transition has one outcome (§58). -/
theorem Guarded.det {σ : Type} {Pre : Prop} {eff : σ} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 σ}
    (h₁ : Guarded Pre eff o₁) (h₂ : Guarded Pre eff o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction

/-- The `ok` outcome of a guarded transition: the preconditions hold and the state is the effect
(§58). -/
theorem Guarded.ok_iff {σ : Type} {Pre : Prop} {eff s' : σ} :
    Guarded Pre eff (.ok s') ↔ Pre ∧ s' = eff :=
  ⟨fun h => by cases h; exact ⟨‹_›, rfl⟩, fun ⟨h, e⟩ => e ▸ .ok h⟩

/-- The `reject` outcome of a guarded transition: the preconditions fail (§58). -/
theorem Guarded.reject_iff {σ : Type} {Pre : Prop} {eff : σ} :
    Guarded Pre eff .reject ↔ ¬ Pre :=
  ⟨fun h => by cases h; assumption, fun h => .reject h⟩

-- what `rewind_ok_iff` does not state: under its right-hand side, `ok` is the only outcome
theorem rewind_only_ok {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (hr : DReach k statics D)
    {j : Nat} {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {m : Mark}
    (hc : LiveMark j st m ∧ AdminRight D.kern st ∧
        ∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), D.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
          st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x → l ∈ y.footprint → l ∉ above st m)
    (o : Outcome3 DState) (ho : RewindStep k j m D o) : ∃ D', o = .ok D' := by
  obtain ⟨D₀, h₀⟩ := (rewind_ok_iff hr hst).2 hc
  cases h₀ with
  | ok h₁ _ _ hsp₀ hrl₀ =>
    rw [hst] at h₁; cases h₁
    cases ho with
    | noStack h => rw [hst] at h; cases h
    | dead h hm => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hc.1 hm
    | static h _ ha => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hc.2.1 ha
    | split h _ _ hsp => rw [hst] at h; cases h; cases Guarded.det hsp hsp₀
    | release h _ _ hsp hrl =>
      rw [hst] at h; cases h
      cases Guarded.det hsp hsp₀
      cases Guarded.det hrl hrl₀
    | ok => exact ⟨_, rfl⟩

#print axioms rewind_only_ok
